_comment: Unit Roadmap spec. Unit title, phase and section titles come from courses/chemistry/DECISIONS.md; do not add them here. 'measured' must agree with DECISIONS.md 'Assessment shape'.
big_idea: A chemical name and a chemical formula hold the same information in two forms. Students use what they know about **bond type** and **ion charges** to move between the name and the formula, following one set of rules instead of memorizing compounds one at a time.
builds_on: Reference packet: periodic table, polyatomic ions
standards_source: Ohio Learning Standards for Science (2018) · Chemistry

ican: I can **classify** a compound as ionic or covalent from the elements it contains.
I can **use** Greek prefixes to name binary covalent compounds.
I can **write** the formula of a covalent compound from its name.
I can **explain** that a polyatomic ion is a group of covalently bonded atoms that carries an overall charge.
I can **identify** common polyatomic ions by name, formula, and charge, using the reference packet when needed.
I can **recognize** patterns in oxyanion names ([[-ate / -ite,]] [[per- / hypo-]]).
I can **predict** main-group ion charges from the periodic table and **balance** charges to write ionic formulas.
I can **work out** a transition metal's charge from a formula and show it with a Roman numeral.
I can **name and write formulas** for ionic compounds, including those with polyatomic ions, using parentheses correctly.
I can **recognize** an acid from its formula.
I can **name** binary acids and oxyacids using the [[hydro-, -ic,]] and [[-ous]] rules.
I can **write** the formula of an acid from its name.

standards_key: properties and trends; used here to predict ion charges.
ionic, polar/nonpolar covalent, metallic bonding; polyatomic ions.
formula writing, nomenclature, models and shapes.
